claims.body: The Avalanche’s defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much. Colorado is one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Minnesota is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Avalanche’s defensemen jump into the play.

notes.text: Nathan MacKinnon is out (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Nelson has taken his spot beside Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Nečas. That line has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 35:46 together, up from 55% with MacKinnon.
Cale Makar returned in their last game after missing 3 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Mike Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 16.
Zachary L'Heureux is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, down from 36% with his old team last season.

Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 52:02 together, about what it had with Hughes (56%).

Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 48% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 75:11 together, about what it had with Määttä (48%).
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 34% last season.

stakes: The Avalanche go in tied for third in the Central with 31 points, 10 points behind the Wild, first.

MIN.head: Too close to call
MIN.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Minnesota will be without Hughes. Then again, Minnesota has home-ice advantage, and Colorado will be without MacKinnon. The Wild can tip it if they keep dangerous shots away.

story.head: Kaprizov’s favorite opponent
paras: The Wild (18-4-5) lost 4-3 to Utah on Wednesday. The Avalanche have won two in a row, the last a 6-0 rout of Montréal. Two of the league’s best teams meet. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Avs third (tied for tenth in the NHL) and the Wild first (tied for first). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
The Avalanche’s record (.646) is about what their chances are worth. The Wild’s record (.759) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.635), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Avalanche do a lot of their shooting from distance (most), play the league’s fastest games (1st) and throw a lot of pucks at the net (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.00 goals a game, the second most in the league. As for the Wild, they draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). They also block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), so the Wild are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Avalanche’s shots. Minnesota has allowed 2.26 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. The Avalanche’s defensemen shoot a lot, and the Wild’s not so much.

Martin Nečas (11 G / 18 A / 29 P in 24 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring, and Artturi Lehkonen (16 G / 7 A / 23 P in 24 GP) has a team-high 16 goals, sixth in the NHL. Kirill Kaprizov (19 G / 30 A / 49 P in 27 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is second in the NHL, with twelve points in his last five games and a point in eight straight games against Colorado.
Mackenzie Blackwood (12-4-1 / .910 SV% in 17 GS) is expected to start for Colorado, and Filip Gustavsson (1-0-0 / .917 SV% in 1 GS) for Minnesota.

The Wild are newly without Quinn Hughes, and have been without Olli Määttä since Nov 14.
